question:
How can I pass the name of the current model using {{this}} as a parameter for a macro in a config function?

I have tried a couple of options and none of them works. model/Table1.sql

{{ config(post_hook= calculate_test("{{this}}") ) }}

macro/calculate_test.sql

{% macro calculate_test(tableN) %}
   
    {%- set tableName = tableN -%}

    {% set sql %}

        SELECT 
            COUNT(*) as cnt
        FROM {{ tableName }}

    {% endset %}

    {% set results = run_query(sql) %}

{% endmacro %}

The error is:
title: How can I use {{this}} as a parameter in a dbt jinja macro?
answer:
You can pass in the keyword this (no braces or apostrophes) to your macro signature and it will get substituted when it's called. This means, you can create the following post_hook statement:

{{ config(
    post_hook="{{ my_macro(this)}}"
) }}

And then call it inside your macro like any other argument:

{% macro my_macro(table_name) %}

    {{ log(table_name, info=True) }}
    /* logs the table name for the model the post_hook originated from  */

{% endmacro %}

this works like any other argument, so you can still pass in multiple args to your macro with this just being one of them:

{{ config(
    post_hook="{{ my_macro(this, 'arg2', 'arg3', ...)}}"
) }}
